{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ks-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"e00765146d4b99e92004c650f1c586c01bc574e60c19917c7fe7139cddbae01e","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ks-class-c:lineage:46","source_registry_sha256":"c7fb2073a9e8bb6a73d0151458fe04991b703d84f882b00a01bedfcea433c383","source_liveness_sha256":"94328be42cc10cf86af8e486b41bc40c72c45e4700d27b9b46d1f3d2feac7bb6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Special driving situations","heading":"C2 — Special driving situations","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Special driving situations

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A92
In work zones, monitor surrounding traffic, obey signs and flaggers, reduce speed as needed and increase following space. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A92
Work-zone lane patterns may change daily; do not ignore familiar long-term signs. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A92
The handbook recommends moving to the appropriate lane at the first notice of an approaching work zone when possible. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A92
Use added caution at night in a work zone even when workers are absent. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A92
When possible, position the vehicle away from the side occupied by workers or equipment. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A92
Some roadwork moves along the road, including painting, patching and mowing; continue obeying signs until the end-of-work notice. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A92
Allow extra travel time for work-zone delays or choose an alternate route when possible. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A92
Do not swerve into opposing traffic or off the road to avoid an animal. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A92
An abrupt animal-avoidance maneuver may cause a more severe crash; maintaining vehicle control is the priority before, during and after impact. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A92
The handbook recommends additional animal caution at dawn and dusk and during October through December. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A92
Be alert at deer-crossing signs, which identify areas with a history of deer-vehicle collisions. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A92
Search well ahead and to both sides for animals, including reflected eye shine at night near woods and water. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A92
Slow near roadside animals because they may change direction abruptly and other deer may follow. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A92
Hazard flashers can warn other drivers of animals on or beside the road. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A92
When time permits avoiding an animal, reduce speed, tap the brakes to warn followers and use the horn. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A92
With no vehicle close behind, the handbook permits hard braking to avoid an animal while avoiding wheel lock and skidding. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A92
If striking an animal is unavoidable, keep control and remain on the road rather than swerving. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A93
Report a collision with a large animal, such as a deer or farm animal, to police. [A93]
Source: [A93 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A93
If a struck animal is a pet and homes are nearby, try to notify its owner when possible without entering anyone's home. [A93]
Source: [A93 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A93
Pets can enter the roadway in residential, rural and farm areas. [A93]
Source: [A93 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0093]

Misconceptions: An empty rural road still has hazards; an apparently shallow flooded road may be washed out; absence of work-zone workers does not cancel signs; swerving around an animal can cause a worse collision.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: surface, sight, space, escape. It organizes hazard checks without adding a driving rule.
Glossary: Distinguish gravel traction, bridge grating, glare, flash flooding, mobile work zones and animal-avoidance control using the source-bound facts.
Dynamic facts: Temporary controls change with roadwork, and weather changes traction and visibility. Edition-bound distances, statistics and unresolved maneuvers require issuer refresh or explicit debt resolution.
